headline: India's RAW chief's Dhaka visit 'normal engagement', says Dr Zahed
summary: PM's information adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman clarifies that the visit of India's intelligence chief is part of regular activities and there is no cause for speculation.
details: Prime Minister's information adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the visit of India's Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief to Dhaka is part of regular activities. He emphasized that there is no reason for speculation regarding the visit.

Dr Zahed explained that the RAW chief arrived in Dhaka from China and will meet with his Bangladeshi counterparts. He noted that Bangladesh's intelligence chief had also previously visited India for similar meetings.

The adviser further asserted that the behavior of Indian agencies in Bangladesh will no longer be as it was during Sheikh Hasina's tenure. He stressed that interactions must reflect the respect due to an independent and sovereign nation.

During the press briefing, Dr Zahed also commented on cricketer Shakib Al Hasan, stating that while he may be a good player, his past associations with the former regime are problematic. He noted that Shakib can return if he accepts legal obligations.

Regarding former PM Sheikh Hasina, Dr Zahed stated that if she returns to Bangladesh, she will be provided full security to undergo judicial proceedings. He emphasized that the country will not tolerate another 'mafia regime'.

The government is also planning to take school students to museums, including the July Uprising Museum, to learn about the history of the mass uprising. This initiative aims to educate the youth on the struggle for democracy.
Additionally, the government is drafting a new policy for the import, storage, and distribution of refined fuel by the private sector to ensure uninterrupted energy security by 2026.
caption:
India's RAW chief is in Dhaka for 'normal engagement'. PM's information adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman says there's no room for speculation.

Prime Minister's information adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the visit of India's Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief to Dhaka is part of regular activities. He emphasized that there is no reason for speculation regarding the visit.

Dr Zahed explained that the RAW chief arrived in Dhaka from China and will meet with his Bangladeshi counterparts. He noted that Bangladesh's intelligence chief had also previously visited India for similar meetings.

The adviser further asserted that the behavior of Indian agencies in Bangladesh will no longer be as it was during Sheikh Hasina's tenure. He stressed that interactions must reflect the respect due to an independent and sovereign nation.

During the press briefing, Dr Zahed also commented on cricketer Shakib Al Hasan, stating that while he may be a good player, his past associations with the former regime are problematic. He noted that Shakib can return if he accepts legal obligations.

Regarding former PM Sheikh Hasina, Dr Zahed stated that if she returns to Bangladesh, she will be provided full security to undergo judicial proceedings. He emphasized that the country will not tolerate another 'mafia regime'.

The government is also planning to take school students to museums, including the July Uprising Museum, to learn about the history of the mass uprising. This initiative aims to educate the youth on the struggle for democracy.

Additionally, the government is drafting a new policy for the import, storage, and distribution of refined fuel by the private sector to ensure uninterrupted energy security by 2026.

headline_marked: Presidential election: [[President to be elected by open vote]] of MPs
headline: Presidential election: President to be elected by open vote of MPs
summary: The Election Commission has held a preparatory meeting at the Parliament House to finalize the process for the upcoming presidential election.
details: The Election Commission has held a preparatory meeting with Acting Speaker Barrister Kaiser Kamal at the Parliament House to discuss the overall preparations for the presidential election.
According to the law, the presidential election will be conducted through an open vote by the members of Parliament, rather than a secret ballot.
Each Member of Parliament (MP) will have only one vote. The Election Commission will prepare the necessary number of ballot papers, each consisting of a counterfoil and an outer foil.
To cast a vote, an MP must first sign the counterfoil of their specific ballot paper to collect it. They then sign their full name next to the preferred candidate's name on the outer foil.

Unlike secret ballots, there is no 'tick mark' or 'seal' used. The voter's signature serves as the vote, making the process transparent and public as it is the signature that identifies who they voted for.
The process follows the rules of the Rules of Procedure of the National Parliament, seorang member's assigned 'division number' is used on the ballot papers for identification.
